title: Is Sycophancy a Form of In-Context Updating?
abstract: arXiv:2610.28325v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Factual sycophancy, a language model's deference to a user's false beliefs, is usually understood as a bid for the user's approval at the expense of truthfulness. We argue that this framing over-emphasizes the user and propose viewing sycophancy as a failure within the broader and generally useful process of in-context updating, by which models revise their answers based on information supplied during an interaction. We support this view with behavioral and mechanistic evidence. First, models' responses to user claims sit within a broader pattern of source-sensitive updating. They revise their answers in response to information attributed to external sources as well, more so when it appears better supported, and their deference to the user persists even when no user approval is at stake. Second, the internal components that support deference to the user are also causally important for in-context updating more broadly. Our results suggest

translated_title: 谄媚是上下文内更新的一种形式吗？
translated_abstract: 事实性谄媚，即语言模型对用户错误信念的顺从，通常被理解为一种以牺牲真实性为代价来博取用户认可的行为。我们认为这种框架过度强调了用户的作用，并提出将谄媚视为“上下文内更新”（in-context updating）这一更广泛且普遍有用的过程中的失败表现——上下文内更新是指模型根据交互过程中提供的信息修改其回答的机制。我们通过行为层面和机制层面的证据支持这一观点。首先，模型对用户断言的回应处于更广泛的“来源敏感更新”模式之中：模型也会根据归属于外部来源的信息修改其回答，当信息看起来有更好的支持时修改幅度更大，并且即使没有任何用户认可的风险存在，模型对用户的顺从依然持续。其次，支持对用户顺从的内部组件对于更广泛的上下文内更新也具有因果上的重要性。我们的结果表明……
tldr: 该论文提出谄媚不应被理解为单纯讨好用户的行为，而是模型“上下文内更新”机制的一种失败表现，并通过行为和机制证据证明模型对用户及外部来源信息的顺从遵循同一套内部更新机制。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that sycophancy is not merely a bid for user approval but a failure within the broader process of in-context updating, supported by behavioral and mechanistic evidence that model deference to users and external sources relies on the same internal updating mechanisms.
